items.title: James Lincoln Collier interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 14, 2007
items.q: some agent, Lynn Nesbit who went on to become quite a well known agent, Lynn suggested I start doing this.

ctx.x: They would call you with assignments or would you submit ideas?

It worked both ways. I mean you’re always looking, you’ve got to make sure you’ve got some work. So if they called you great. Hey Jim would you be interested in thus and so. If they didn’t call you you’d be out hustling. Hey Charlie I’m going to be in town on Wednesday I thought I might drop by, whatever, see what you can get. But I never wanted to do that. My father had been in the magazine business, my uncle I mean knew a lot of that magazine business. It wasn’t interesting. I mean I take that back. You did a…

difficult and is interesting and is challenging and still make a living from it. And that to me has been the great blessing, that I could write and have reached the point now and have been at this point for some years where I can call my own shots. I write when I want to write and I generally manage to get paid for enough of it so that I can keep going with it.
